display.purpose: Monument section titles at peer scale: clamp(2.5rem, 5.5vw, 4.75rem), 40px at 390 and 76px at 1440.

display-name.purpose: Case-study names over their photos, authored casing: clamp(2.25rem, 5vw, 4.25rem), 36px at 390 and 68px at 1440.

numeral.purpose: Process step numbers in dust grey.

label.purpose: Small tracked uppercase headings that name their own block, and term labels.

kicker.purpose: One instance only: 'Software that does the heavy lifting' above the hero H1, ice cyan. Dan's deliberate override of the eyebrow ban; no other kickers or eyebrows.

motion.name: spring-settle
motion.purpose: Entrances: hero stagger, testimonial swap, process numerals, menu links. Soft settle, no visible bounce.

motion.name: spring-press
motion.purpose: Press feedback on buttons, step buttons and CTA links, always through the shared PressButton / PressLink components.

motion.name: stagger-in
motion.value: react-spring useTrail, translateY 12px to 0, no opacity change, settle spring
motion.purpose: Hero entrance (kicker, H1, lede, actions) and mobile menu links. Content is visible from the first frame; it only rises.

motion.name: stagger-step
motion.purpose: Delay between process numerals rising on first entry.

motion.name: hero-zoom
motion.purpose: Slow zoom of the hero nebula; the only loop.

motion.name: scroll-reveal
motion.value: animation-timeline: view(); range entry 0% to entry 60%; opacity 0.15 to 1, translateY 1.5rem to 0
motion.purpose: Monument titles entering the viewport, where supported.

motion.name: hover-transition
motion.purpose: Link, button and icon hover states.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Not applied under reduce: hero zoom, scroll reveal, smooth in-page scrolling (motion-safe:scroll-smooth), and the Sheet overlay, Sheet panel and Accordion open animations. Springs skip to end state (react-spring Globals.skipAnimation, following live changes); hover nudges motion-safe only.

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Monolith"**

A night ground, one cold accent, and large uppercase titles at peer scale standing in front of real telescope photographs. The site borrows the restraint of a large observatory's public face: almost nothing on the page is decorative, so the photographs of facilities Dan's work touched and the large uppercase section titles carry the whole atmosphere. One retro-future signature, the Monument title, does the shouting; everything else is quiet, small, and set in a humanist grotesk.

Density is low and vertical. Sections are separated by space and hairline rules, never by background bands or cards. Photography is full-bleed or plainly cropped, always credited in a caption under it, and the hero nebula is the only image that moves. Motion is slow (a 60 s zoom) or small (springs that settle in under half a second); nothing loops for decoration.

The theme is dark-only. There is no light mode and no theme switch, and every text color is chosen to pass WCAG AA on the night ground.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-only ground with a single ice-cyan accent.
Monument titles at peer scale (76px at most), uppercase for generic words only.
Square everything: zero radius on every surface and control.
Credited observatory photography as the only imagery.
Hairline rules and space as the only separators.
Soft spring micro-motion, fully disabled under reduced motion.

rules.name: The One Cold Light Rule
rules.body: Ice cyan is the only chromatic color in the interface. Color in the page beyond it comes from the photographs.

rules.name: The No Bands Rule
rules.body: Sections never get their own background color. They separate by space and a hairline.

rules.name: The Monument Scale Rule
rules.body: A Monument title sits at the scale of its peers (observatory and studio sites top out at 70-80px on desktop and 35-60px on mobile), never filling the viewport width. Its size is a fixed clamp per role (Display for section titles, Display name for case-study names), not measured from the container, and it stays left aligned and larger than the service titles at every width. Long titles wrap naturally and balance, so "Start a project" takes two lines on a phone and one on a desktop. A bottom padding of 0.12em keeps descenders inside a clipping photo band. No negative margins, no viewport-overflowing sizes, no horizontal translation.

rules.name: The Casing Rule
rules.body: Uppercase is applied by CSS and only to generic words: Monument section titles, the H1, service titles, process step titles, labels, menu links. Anything containing a proper name keeps its authored casing: institutions, case-study names (pyINDI, never PYINDI), organizations, publication titles, testimonial attributions. When uppercase text contains a mixed-case acronym, the text stays uppercase and only the acronym keeps its casing ("PYTHON LIBRARIES & APIs"); route such text through Caps. Generic titles are authored in sentence case in source and transformed; proper-name Monuments are not transformed.

rules.name: The One Kicker Rule
rules.body: The hero line "Software that does the heavy lifting" is the site's only kicker: a tracked uppercase ice-cyan line above the H1 (0.7rem at 0.2em on mobile, 0.75rem at 0.32em on desktop). This is Dan's deliberate override of impeccable's eyebrow ban, decided after the finish review, because the tagline is the brand line and its pun lands through the M27 caption. No other eyebrow labels are allowed anywhere: a small tracked label may be the heading of its own block, but never a tag stacked above another heading.

rules.name: The Flat Night Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats. Separation is space, a hairline, or a fade to the ground.

dos: Do use ice cyan as the only accent, with dark ink on any cyan fill.
Do separate sections with space and hairlines on the one night ground.
Do use the Monument component for a new section title so it takes the shared Display size; never size one by hand.
Do author generic titles in sentence case and let CSS uppercase them; route uppercase text with a mixed-case acronym through Caps.
Do keep proper names, institutions, and brands in their authored casing (pyINDI, NSF NOIRLab, Caltech / IPAC, SPHEREx).
Do credit every photo in a caption and in the footer credits list.
Do show CC BY-SA photos unaltered: CSS cropping (object-fit, aspect ratio, overflow) only.
Do keep every new animation behind the shared motion module or a reduced-motion query, and start content visible.
Do keep every text color at WCAG AA on the night ground and every control boundary at 3:1.
donts: Don't add a light theme, theme switch, or second accent color.
Don't add eyebrow labels or kickers; the hero tagline is the single sanctioned kicker.
Don't uppercase a proper name or brand, and don't crop, overflow, translate, or negatively-margin a Monument title.

Don't retint, recolor, filter, mask, dim, or overlay a CC BY-SA photo (MMT, VATT, Lowell Discovery Telescope); masks, dimming, and gradients are only for CC BY and public-domain images such as the M27 hero and the case-study bands.
Don't round corners or add shadows.
Don't use card grids or background bands to group content.
Don't add springs on scroll position, decorative loops, horizontal title drift, WebGL, video, or canvas animation.
